newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse recovers, but volume to stay thin.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse recovers, but volume to stay thin.

text.p: The Brussels bourse along with others inb Europe on Monday shrugged off last week's comments by the Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan and regained some lost ground with dealers expecting volume to remain thin.
"Europe and the U.S. are in a different stage in the economic cycle. If it rains in the U.S. it drips in Europe," one said.
He added European fundamentals did need not any adjusting as inflation was under control and interest rates remained low.
The Bel-20 index closed up 0.75 percent, or 14.01 points, to 1,885.47.
One dealer said, "The Belgian stock market always lags the European bourses because of its low liquidity and being considered a relatively small market in the Morgan Stanley capital markets survey."

Dealers and analysts were keeping their eyes on utility holding company Tractebel after rumours circulated that its board of directors would decide on Thursday whether to merge the company with its Powerfin unit.
"This will be a very good transaction for Tractebel, they will be able to simplify their structure," said analyst Maud Watelet of Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
Tractebel closed up 100 francs at 14,600 francs and Powerfin rose 55 francs to 4,840 francs.
Among cyclicals, cement maker CBR regained some strength after having lagged the index in recent days, closing up 50 francs at 2,700.
"CBR has fallen sharply in recent weeks with investors taking profits but now we're seeing some buybacks and the expiry of its put warrant has helped the share," said one dealer.
